label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences whose first token is in a preferred set
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (99% of activation mass; delimiter-phase recall 0.98). Within the delimiter it is gated by sequence length: rate is about 45% at L=9, 25% at L=8, 5% at L=7 and essentially zero for L<=6, with L=9 carrying 66% of mass. It is further modulated by the first original token, which is also the token output at the delimiter step: high firing rates for j, s, y, r, n, h, e, z, g, k, b, digit 1 (about 0.5-0.8 precision at L>=8), moderate for f, p, t, and near-zero for o, d, u, w, q, c, m, x, digits 0/2/3. Small residual activity (about 1% of mass) on the last original token for L=9, mostly when that token is d/o/u. Does not fire during the copy phase or for early original steps. Remaining variance among long, preferred-first-token sequences was not captured by any simple token condition, so precision stays around 0.6.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: j, s, y, r, n, b; least: q, c, d, o) and the second original token (most: s, y, z, e, j, n; least: 0, u, d, o); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=9, L=9 & t=8.
